title: Purnima vs Amavasya: full moon and new moon in Vedic astrology | Ask Tota
description: Purnima is the full moon tithi, Amavasya the new moon. How tithis work, why eclipses only fall on these days, and the festivals each one carries.
og_description: Full moon, new moon, and the 12 degree rule that defines every tithi. Why eclipses only happen on these two days, and the festivals that follow them.
h1: purnima and amavasya: the two days the whole hindu calendar hangs on
dek: the full moon and the new moon are the two ends of every lunar month. in the vedic calendar they are tithis, defined by exactly how far the moon is from the sun. eclipses can only happen on them, many of the biggest festivals sit on them, and each is said to favour different kinds of action.

llms_desc: what Purnima (full moon) and Amavasya (new moon) are as tithis in the Hindu lunar calendar, how tithis are defined by 12 degree Sun-Moon elongation, why solar eclipses fall only on Amavasya and lunar eclipses only on Purnima, major festivals on each, traditional observances, and myths.

faq.a: the full moon tithi, the 15th and last tithi of shukla paksha, the waxing fortnight. it is when the moon is 180 degrees from the sun and fully lit.
the new moon tithi, the last tithi of krishna paksha, the waning fortnight. the moon and sun are together in the sky, so the moon is dark.

a lunar day, the time the moon takes to gain 12 degrees on the sun. there are 30 tithis in a lunar month, 15 waxing and 15 waning. because the moon's speed varies, a tithi lasts roughly 19 to 26 hours.

faq.q: what is the difference between purnima and amavasya?
faq.a: purnima is the full moon, with the moon opposite the sun; amavasya is the new moon, with the moon conjunct the sun. purnima is traditionally linked with fullness and celebration, amavasya with ancestors, introspection and endings.

faq.q: why do eclipses only happen on purnima or amavasya?
faq.a: a solar eclipse needs the moon between earth and sun, which only happens at new moon. a lunar eclipse needs earth between sun and moon, which only happens at full moon. both also need the moon near rahu or ketu.
it is traditionally avoided for starting new ventures, marriages and auspicious ceremonies, but it is highly auspicious for ancestor rites, spiritual practice and some festivals, including diwali.

faq.q: is purnima good for starting new things?
faq.a: purnima is widely considered auspicious and is used for vows, fasts, worship and many festivals. for specific undertakings astrologers still check the full muhurat, not the tithi alone.
guru purnima, raksha bandhan, sharad purnima, kartik purnima, holi on phalguna purnima and buddha purnima, among many others.
diwali, mahalaya amavasya at the end of pitru paksha, mauni amavasya and somvati amavasya, when a new moon falls on a monday.

faq.q: does the full moon affect behaviour?
faq.a: it is a popular belief, but large studies of hospital admissions, crime and emergency calls have generally not found reliable full moon effects on behaviour.

faq.q: why do some calendars count the month from purnima?
faq.a: india uses two systems. amanta months end on amavasya, common in the south and west. purnimanta months end on purnima, common in the north. the festivals fall on the same days; only the month names shift.

faq.q: what should i do on amavasya?
faq.a: traditional observances include tarpan for ancestors, charity, quiet reflection, and in some traditions fasting. it is treated as a day for completing and releasing rather than beginning.
